problems.title: Remove an interval from an intersection
problems.question: A=[−5,7),B=(−19.9/4,0),C=[−1,4/3). Count integers in (A∩B)∖C.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: First intersect A and B, then remove all points in C.
steps: A∩B=(−4.975,0). Removing C leaves (−4.975,−1), containing exactly −4,−3,−2.

problems.title: Count integers between square roots
problems.question: How many integers lie strictly between −√199 and √600?
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
steps: The permitted integers run from −14 through 24, inclusive. Count=24−(−14)+1=39.

problems.title: Equivalent inequalities have identical solution sets
problems.question: Which are equivalent: I |x|≥x, II |x|<x, III |x|≤−x, IV |x+199|≤199?
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Solve each inequality as a set of real inputs.
steps: I holds for every real x. II has no solutions. III gives x≤0. IV gives −398≤x≤0.
These are four different sets, so no pair is equivalent.

problems.title: A person in a building shadow
problems.question: A 20 m building and a 2 m person share a shadow endpoint 5 m beyond the person. Find the person’s distance from the building, as drawn.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Similar right triangles have height/base ratio $20/(d+5)=2/5$.
steps: The building shadow length is 50 m. Subtract the person’s 5 m shadow to obtain d=45 m.

problems.title: Incircle contact points in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: The distance between incircle contact points on the equal sides is 6; base is 10. Find the perimeter.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Equal tangent lengths and similar triangles at the apex.
steps: Let each equal side be L. Each base-vertex tangent length is 5, so apex-to-contact length is L−5.
The contact chord is parallel to the base by symmetry. Similarity gives (L−5)/L=6/10, hence L=12.5. Perimeter=2L+10=35.

problems.title: A rational radicand must be nonnegative
problems.question: Find the real domain of √[−2023/(m+199)].
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: The denominator is nonzero, and a square-root radicand must be nonnegative.
steps: The numerator is strictly negative. The quotient is positive exactly when m+199<0, so m<−199. Equality is undefined.

problems.title: Count rational radical expressions
problems.question: Classify I 3√7·2√14; II (3/4)√24·(2/3)√6; III √9·√0.9·√0.09·√0.009; IV (√10+√5)²; V 2√18+3√8+3√32−√50; VI √10·√20·√40·√80.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: For nonnegative inputs, $\sqrt u\sqrt v=\sqrt{uv}$; simplify square factors.
steps: I=42√2 is irrational. II=(1/2)√144=6 is rational. III=√0.006561=0.081 is rational.
IV=15+10√2 is irrational. V=(6+6+12−5)√2=19√2 is irrational. VI=√640000=800 is rational.
Exactly II,III,VI are rational.

problems.title: Identify a region defined by three half-planes
problems.question: What figure is described by y−3x<7,2x+y≤7,y≥−19?
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Find the three boundary-line intersections.
steps: The upper boundaries meet at (0,7). The lower horizontal line meets them at (−26/3,−19) and (13,−19).
The region is triangular. The edge on y=3x+7 is excluded because that inequality is strict; the other two edges are included except where they meet the excluded edge.
problems.answer: A triangle with one edge excluded.

problems.title: A parallel cut and a side difference
problems.question: D∈AB,AD:DB=3:5, DE∥BC with E∈AC. BC−DE=20. Find DE.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Similarity gives $DE/BC=AD/AB=3/8$.
steps: Then BC−DE=(5/8)BC=20, so BC=32 and DE=12.

problems.title: Parallel sections through trisection points
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 6,12. Its leg is trisected, and the two parallel cross-sections have lengths MN,KL. Find their sum.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Parallel cross-section length varies linearly between base lengths.
steps: At one third and two thirds of the height, lengths are 6+(12−6)/3=8 and 6+2(12−6)/3=10. Their sum is 18.

problems.title: Two incompatible numerical bounds
problems.question: Which listed x solves 1<0.5x+1≤1.041 and 0.083≤x<0.3?
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: The first pair gives $0<x\le0.082$.
steps: The second requires x≥0.083, strictly above the first upper bound. Their intersection is empty, so no listed value works.

problems.title: One inequality’s solutions must imply another
problems.question: Count negative integers a such that every x satisfying x−6a>199 also satisfies 2x−3a≥0.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Require $(199+6a,\infty)\subseteq[3a/2,\infty)$, equivalent to $199+6a\ge3a/2$.
steps: This simplifies to a≥−398/9≈−44.222. The negative integer values are −44 through −1, exactly 44.
Equality of the thresholds is allowed: a strict lower bound on x still implies the non-strict bound.

problems.title: Order radicals by simplifying nested squares
problems.question: Order a=1/(4+√3), b=√(7−4√3), c=√[(√3−1)/(√3+1)].
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: $b=2-\sqrt3$ and $c=\sqrt{2-\sqrt3}$.
steps: b≈0.268 and c=√b≈0.518, so b<c. To compare a,b, multiply b by positive 4+√3: (2−√3)(4+√3)=5−2√3>1, since √3<2.
Thus b>1/(4+√3)=a. The order is a<b<c.

problems.title: An intercept line crosses a parallelogram diagonal
problems.question: K∈AB,AK:KB=2:3; M∈AD,AM:MD=4:1. In parallelogram ABCD, line KM meets AC at P. Find AP:PC.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Use coordinates relative to the two side vectors: $K=(2/5,0)$, $M=(0,4/5)$, $P=(t,t)$.
steps: The intercept equation is u/(2/5)+v/(4/5)=1. At P it gives (5/2)t+(5/4)t=1, so t=4/15.
Thus AP:PC=t:(1−t)=4:11.

problems.title: A tangent and a diameter secant
problems.question: A lies outside a circle. AD is tangent; AC passes through the centre to far endpoint C. The outside secant portion is half AD. Find distance(C,line AD):radius.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Power of A: $AD^2=AE\cdot AC$; distance to a line through A scales along ray AC.
steps: Let AE=x and radius r. Then AD=2x and AC=x+2r. Thus 4x²=x(x+2r), giving x=2r/3.
AO=x+r=5r/3 and AC=8r/3. Centre O is distance r from the tangent AD, so C is distance (AC/AO)r=(8/5)r.

problems.title: Keep the sign condition when removing absolute value
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of |x−2|(x−5)=x−2.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: First check x=2; then divide by x−2 in the remaining cases.
steps: x=2 is a root. For x>2, cancellation gives x−5=1, so x=6. For x<2, it gives −(x−5)=1, or x=4, which violates x<2.
The valid roots 2 and 6 sum to 8.

problems.title: Domain checks in three radical equations
problems.question: Find the combined sum of roots of √(x²−1)=√3; √(x−1)√(x+2)=0; (x+6)√(x−9)=0.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Real radicals require nonnegative radicands.
steps: The first has roots ±2, summing to 0. The second has domain x≥1, so only x=1 is a root; x=−2 is excluded.
The third has domain x≥9, so only x=9 is a root; x=−6 is excluded. Combined sum=0+1+9=10.

problems.title: Two absolute-value intervals
problems.question: Count integers k with 8≤|2k+2|≤26.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Divide by 2: $4\le|k+1|\le13$.
steps: k+1 is one of 4,…,13 or −13,…,−4. Each list has ten integers, giving twenty values of k.

problems.title: A perimeter difference and secant power
problems.question: Secants AB,AC from external A meet the circle first at D,E. AD=2,BC=AC=6. Perimeter BDEC exceeds perimeter ADE by 11. Find BD.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Power of A gives $AD\cdot AB=AE\cdot AC$.
steps: Let BD=t,AE=u. Then 2(t+2)=6u, or t=3u−2.
The perimeter difference is t+DE+(6−u)+6−(2+DE+u)=t+10−2u=11, so t=2u+1.
Equating gives u=3 and t=7. All point orders remain valid: AE=3<AC=6 and AB=9>AD=2.

problems.title: Distances from an incircle centre to two vertices
problems.question: A right trapezoid has acute angle 60°. The incircle contact on its slanted leg divides it into a<b; radius is r. Find the sum of centre-to-endpoint distances.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: At angle θ, tangent length $=r\cot(\theta/2)$ and centre-to-vertex distance $=r/\sin(\theta/2)$.
steps: The leg endpoints have angles 60°,120°. Their tangent lengths are √3r=b and r/√3=a.
The centre distances are 2r and 2r/√3=2a. Their sum is 2r+2a.

problems.title: A repeating decimal in a radical inequality
problems.question: Count integers x satisfying √(x−6)<7.2·0.41(6).
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
steps: The right side is 3. The inequality requires 0≤x−6<9, or 6≤x<15. Integers 6 through 14 give nine solutions.

problems.title: Count lattice points in an open triangle
problems.question: Count integer-coordinate points satisfying y>−1,3x−2y>−6,x+y<3.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: For integer y≥0, require $(2y-6)/3<x<3-y$.
steps: For y=0, x=−1,0,1,2 gives 4 points. For y=1, x=−1,0,1 gives 3. For y=2, only x=0 works.
For y≥3 the lower bound is at least the upper bound, giving no points. Total=4+3+1=8.

problems.title: A tangent trapezoid with its centre on a base
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD, AB is tangent at B to the circle through B,C,D. Its centre O lies on base AD=198 and A=30°. Find distance from O to diagonal BD.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: $OB\perp AB$; in right triangle AOB, $r=AO\sin30°=AO/2$.
steps: D is the circle point on AD beyond O, so AD=AO+r=3AO/2=198. Hence AO=132,r=66.
AOB=60°, so BOD=120° because OA and OD are opposite rays. The perpendicular from O to chord BD bisects this central angle.
Its length is r cos60°=66/2=33.

problems.title: A parallelogram on two medians of a right triangle
problems.question: Right triangle ABC has hypotenuse AC=15. M,N are the side midpoints for medians CM,AN; F∈AN,Q∈CM make FMNQ a parallelogram. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Put B=0,A=u,C=v with $u\perp v$; $M=u/2$, $N=v/2$ and $F+N=M+Q$.
steps: Write F=(1−t)u+(t/2)v. The parallelogram identity gives Q=(1/2−t)u+(1+t)v/2. Requiring Q on CM yields t=1/3.
Thus FM=|u+v|/6. Orthogonality gives |u+v|=|u−v|=AC=15, so FM=2.5. Also MN=AC/2=7.5.

problems.title: Diagonals of a quadrilateral of four midpoints
problems.question: A trapezoid’s angles at the longer base sum to 90°. Form a quadrilateral from the two base midpoints and the two diagonal midpoints. Find its diagonal-length ratio.
problems.idea: Translate the intervals or geometry into equations, retaining endpoints and domain restrictions.
formulas: Let base difference be Δ, height h and left overhang x. The angle condition gives $h^2=x(\Delta-x)$.
steps: The diagonal-midpoint segment has length Δ/2 and is parallel to the bases. The base-midpoint segment has horizontal component x−Δ/2 and vertical component h.
Its squared length is (x−Δ/2)²+h²=Δ²/4, using h²=x(Δ−x). Thus its length is also Δ/2.
These are the two diagonals of the midpoint quadrilateral, so their ratio is 1:1.
